title: Tree Diameter
statement:
Find the length of the longest path between any two nodes of a binary tree.

Contract
- A `TreeNode` has an `int val`, a `left` child, and a `right` child (either may be null).
- A path moves along parent-child edges and never visits a node twice. It may start and end at any nodes and does not have to pass through the root.
- Return the number of edges on the longest such path.
- A null tree and a single-node tree both return 0.
- Node values are irrelevant. Do not modify the tree.

Examples
- `diameter(null)` returns `0`.
- A single node returns `0`.
- Level order `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` returns `3`, from node 4 up through 2 and 1 down to 3.
hints: The best path has a highest node; it goes down into that node's left subtree and down into its right subtree. That highest node is not necessarily the root.
For any node, the longest path whose top is that node has length (deepest descent on the left) + (deepest descent on the right). So you need the height of both children at every node.

Compute heights in one post-order pass, and update a running maximum with left height + right height at each node, instead of recomputing heights for every node. Intended complexity: O(n) time; O(h) recursion stack (no heap allocation beyond one counter), where h is the tree height.
inputSyntax: Input: tree in level order with null for gaps, for example: 1 2 3 4 5
